pr_body:
# Objective

Fixes #14980

## Solution

Only iterate over archetypes containing the component.

## Alternatives

Additionally, for each archetype, cache how many observers are watching one of its components & use this to speed up the check for each affected archetype ([implemented here](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/commit/55c89aa0334975642bbd8978d97fe66c4970078a)).
Benchmarking showed this to lead only to a minor speedup.

## Testing

There's both already a test checking that observers don't run after being despawned as well as a regression test for the bug that necessitates the check this PR optimizes.
pr_comments:
> There was an existing comment labeled SAFETY that concerned absence of panics rather than the usual sense of safety. Was that deliberate?

Yeah, this shouldn't have been formatted like that.

Benchmark: https://gist.github.com/SpecificProtagonist/27fce27a8acb4e7a4156bcb18a707fd9

With max_simultanous_observers = 1
```
Main:
  Time (mean ± σ):     22.161 s ±  1.670 s    [User: 21.957 s, System: 0.175 s]
  Range (min … max):   18.085 s … 24.108 s    10 runs

by_component lookup:
  Time (mean ± σ):      7.241 s ±  0.110 s    [User: 7.080 s, System: 0.151 s]
  Range (min … max):    7.087 s …  7.514 s    10 runs

With cached count:
  Time (mean ± σ):      6.733 s ±  0.051 s    [User: 6.563 s, System: 0.160 s]
  Range (min … max):    6.670 s …  6.836 s    10 runs
```
Also went from 48493 perf samples in `unregister_observers` to 7175.

With max_simultanous_observers = 3
```
Main:
  Time (mean ± σ):     28.726 s ±  0.505 s    [User: 28.211 s, System: 0.472 s]
  Range (min … max):   27.892 s … 29.531 s    10 runs

by_component lookup:
  Time (mean ± σ):     14.106 s ±  0.207 s    [User: 13.664 s, System: 0.426 s]
  Range (min … max):   13.868 s … 14.495 s    10 runs

With cached count:
  Time (mean ± σ):     13.273 s ±  0.394 s    [User: 12.819 s, System: 0.436 s]
  Range (min … max):   12.727 s … 13.916 s    10 runs
```

The main speedup in this benchmark is from using `Archetypes::by_component` instead of iterating over all archetypes.
Caching the number of observers for the archetype also helps a little bit, but may not be worth the maintenance burden, so I'd be happy to remove this from the PR.

> Caching the number of observers for the archetype also helps a little bit, but may not be worth the maintenance burden, so I'd be happy to remove this from the PR.

Let's cut this for now.

issue_context.title: Consider making check for unregistering observers faster
issue_context.body:
> Ouch, that's a painful check. It's needed for correctness though. At some point storing a counter for "how many observers are watching this archetype" and decrementing it is likely to be a good perf optimization, but I'd prefer the simple correctness fix first.

> For context, we use a similar trick in scheduling to track "how many system dependencies remain".

_Originally posted by @alice-i-cecile in https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/pull/14963#pullrequestreview-2267510290_

review_comments:
Should this maybe be a new method on `Archetypes`? Like `fn containing_component(&self, component: ...) -> ...`
I don't like leaking details to the rest of the crate as it will make internal refactorings harder. The principle invoked here is often called "Talk to friends, not to strangers"

That method already exists (`Archetypes::component_index`), but we need to split the mutable borrow because we need to mutably access the archetypes. I could collect the archetype ids into a vec first to avoid that if you prefer?
Ah, I see. No, it's fine then :)
Is this `if` not always true now?
As far as I understand, you can spawn (and despawn) an observer that watches the lifecycle of a component without creating any archetypes containing this component.
